original_question: Let (Omega, mu) be a sigma-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Omega), let a: V x V -> C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, let -A generate the associated bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Omega), and assume that (T(t)) is L-infinity-bounded in the sense that there exists M >= 1 with ||T(t)f||_infinity <= M ||f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega). Must there exist a function g in L-infinity(Omega) with g > 0 mu-almost everywhere and 1/g in L-infinity(Omega) such that ||g T(t)f||_infinity <= ||g f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega) and all t >= 0?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 22 (L∞-contraction for a weight problem), in the setup of Problem 21 (L∞-boundedness problem).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the setting from Problem 21: a σ-finite measure space (Ω,μ), a dense subspace V of L²(Ω), a closed sectorial sesquilinear form a, the associated operator A with -A generating a bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L²(Ω), the L∞-boundedness assumption ||T(t)f||∞ ≤ M||f||∞ on L²(Ω)∩L∞(Ω), and the precise existence question from Problem 22 asking for a weight g ∈ L∞ with g>0 μ-a.e. and 1/g ∈ L∞ such that ||gT(t)f||∞ ≤ ||gf||∞.
missing_details: The paper explicitly works with complex-valued L²-functions.
The sesquilinear form convention is part of the setup: a is linear in the first argument and antilinear in the second.
Sectoriality is stated explicitly: there exists θ ∈ [0,π/2) such that a(u,u) ∈ Σθ := {z ∈ C \ {0} : |arg z| ≤ θ} ∪ {0} for every u ∈ V.
Closedness is defined explicitly: V is complete for the norm ||u||_a = (Re a(u,u) + ||u||²_{L²(Ω)})^{1/2}.
The operator A is introduced via the usual form association on L²(Ω): u ∈ D(A) and Au = h iff u ∈ V and a(u,v) = ⟨h,v⟩ for all v ∈ V.
To match the paper exactly, the target is the pure existence question of Problem 22, not the broader characterization question of Problem 23 and not the construction question of Problem 24.
refined_question: Let (Ω,μ) be a σ-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L²(Ω;C), and let a:V×V→C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, linear in the first argument and antilinear in the second, such that for some θ ∈ [0,π/2) one has a(u,u) ∈ Σθ for every u ∈ V and V is complete for the norm ||u||_a := (Re a(u,u)+||u||²_{L²(Ω)})^{1/2}. Let A be the operator on L²(Ω) associated with a in the usual form sense, so that -A generates the bounded analytic semigroup (T(t))_{t≥0} on L²(Ω). Assume that (T(t))_{t≥0} is L∞-bounded, i.e. there exists M ≥ 1 such that ||T(t)f||∞ ≤ M||f||∞ for all t ≥ 0 and all f ∈ L²(Ω)∩L∞(Ω). Is it then true that there exists a function g ∈ L∞(Ω) with g>0 μ-almost everywhere and g^{-1} ∈ L∞(Ω) such that ||gT(t)f||∞ ≤ ||gf||∞ for all t ≥ 0 and all f ∈ L²(Ω)∩L∞(Ω)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by the form criterion stated in the comments to Problem 21, is it true under the same hypotheses that there exists g ∈ L∞(Ω) with g>0 μ-a.e. and g^{-1} ∈ L∞(Ω) such that for every u ∈ V one has sgn(u)(|u|-g)^+ ∈ V and Re a(u, sgn(u)(|u|-g)^+) ≥ 0, where (|u|-g)^+ denotes the positive part and sgn(u)=u/|u| on {u≠0}?
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 22, not at the broader neighboring Problems 21, 23, or 24. Problem 22 on p. 16 asks exactly whether, in the setting of Problem 21, L∞-boundedness of the semigroup forces the existence of a weight g with g>0 μ-a.e., g^{-1} ∈ L∞, and the weighted L∞-contractivity condition (3). Problem 21 on pp. 14–16 provides the full ambient setup and notation: σ-finite (Ω,μ), dense V ⊆ L²(Ω), complex-valued functions, the linear/antilinear convention for a, the precise sectoriality and closedness assumptions, the associated operator A, the L∞-boundedness condition (1), and the weighted contractivity condition (3). The comments to Problem 21 also explicitly state that (3) is characterized by the form condition (4), which gives the paper-approved alternate formulation. Problem 23 on p. 16 is different: it asks for a characterization of those L∞-bounded semigroups for which such a g exists; your draft does not ask for that broader characterization, so Problem 22 is the nearest official formulation.
